fields.description:
The ESM controller not have logic to block {{.map}} request explicitly ({{import_map}} allow {{.js.map}} as valid suffix by default). The JS is safe only because production build not include sourcemaps, not because there is any real guard for it. But the vendored bundles ({{lib/bundles/}}: React, ReactDOM, {{@moodlehq/design-system}}) are copy from npm as-is, still have {{sourceMappingURL}} comment and the matching {{.js.map}} file also. Because ESM controller and {{import_map}} not reject this, anyone can fetch full unminified source of vendored UI component in production via {{/esm/{revision}/...}}.

*Proposed fix:*

When serving JS file with valid production revision (revision > -1), we use PHP stream filter to strip the {{//# sourceMappingURL=...}} comment before file is deliver to browser.

The filter class will be at {{core\output\requirements\filters\strip_sourcemap_filter}} (extend {{php_user_filter}}), and register + append to the response stream. Filter use {{preg_replace}} to remove {{//# sourceMappingURL=.*}} line on each bucket.

After this in place, we also consider to cache the filtered result so regex not need apply on every request.

We also need to check xsendfile and friends, and if there anything we can/want do to simplify this for Routing. Also need to think if {{.map}} request should be reject outright (not only strip the in-file reference) when revision > -1.

fields.description:
Implement CLI tooling that allows developers to discover and scaffold React component overrides in Moodle themes and plugins.

The initial implementation should be written in JavaScript and integrated with Moodle's existing JavaScript CLI tooling.

h2. Features

h3. Component discovery

The CLI should provide an interactive search experience for discovering React components that can be overridden.

Initially, the search should be limited to {{.tsx}} files within the Moodle codebase.

h3. Component support status

Each discovered component should display a theming support status:

* {{safe}} - explicitly supported for theming
* {{risky}} - theming is allowed, but compatibility is not guaranteed
* {{prohibited}} - should not be themed

If no support metadata exists for a component, the CLI should default to {{risky}}.

Components marked as {{prohibited}} must not be generated by the tooling.

The status names are still up for debate

h3. Override generation

Once a component has been selected, the CLI should generate the appropriate override file in the target theme or plugin.

The generated file should contain scaffold code that allows developers to immediately begin customisation without manually creating the file structure or determining import paths.

h3. Wrap mode

Wrap mode should generate a component that imports and renders the original component, providing a safe extension point for additional behaviour or presentation changes.

h3. Target selection

Before generating an override, the CLI should determine the target theme or plugin.

When the command is executed from the Moodle root directory, the developer should be prompted to select the target theme or plugin from the available candidates.

When the command is executed from within a supported theme or plugin directory, the target may be inferred automatically.

h3. Override mode

Once a component and target have been selected, the CLI should generate the appropriate override file in the target theme or plugin.

The generated file should contain scaffold code that allows developers to immediately begin customisation without manually creating the file structure or determining import paths.

h2. Out of scope

The definition of component support metadata, metadata file format, and classification of components should be tracked separately. This issue focuses on the CLI workflow and code generation.

Until metadata support is implemented, components without metadata should be treated as {{risky}}.

fields.summary: Add React String/Translation component to core using use() and cacheStrings

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: JavaScript
components.description: Anything related to Javascript infrastructure. Specific JS scripts should be handled by the component that the code is in.

fields.description:
h2. Summary

Add a {{String}} React component to core that wraps Moodle's {{core/str}} AMD module using React 19's {{use()}} hook.

h2. Background

The simple approach of passing {{Promise<string>}} directly as a Suspense child works fine for just rendering. But it breaks silently when you need the string value for other things like {{useEffect}}, {{aria-label}}, or any logic. In that case you get a Promise object instead of the real string. The {{use()}} hook fixes this — it makes sure the string is already resolved before the component body runs.

h2. What's included

* {{<String identifier="..." component="..." params="..." />}} — renders a translated string with Suspense fallback support
* {{getString(identifier, component, params)}} — for when you need the string value directly in logic or attributes, used together with {{use()}}
* {{cacheStrings(requests)}} — pre-loads all strings in one batch request upfront, so individual {{getString()}} calls just hit the cache
* {{stringPromiseCache}} — internal cache to give {{use()}} a stable Promise reference across renders, otherwise it suspends forever

h2. Still needed

* Figure out how to mock {{@moodle/lms/core/String}} in Jest, specifically {{getString}} and {{cacheStrings}}

fields.summary: Phpunit and behat fails if a plugin registers own autoloader

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
Phpunit fails when there’s a plugin in the code base that registers its own autoloader in lib.php.

Not sure if this is a real “bug” in the moodle core code or if plugins just should not do something like requiring an own autoloader in the lib.php file. Anyway, plugins might do this, even if it is discouraged, so it makes sense to harden the core code to deal with these cases.

To reproduce:

* git clone [https://github.com/owncloud/moodle-repository_ocis|https://github.com/owncloud/moodle-repository_ocis|smart-link]  public/repository/ocis
* cd public/repository/ocis
* git checkout 42c7f34ab959af0788100ea00113fd6726129f30
* rm phpunit.xml (if exists)
* php public/admin/tool/phpunit/cli/util.php --drop (important and necessary, because afterwards, “allversionshash” cannot be read from config table which then forces caches to be rebuilt and load all plugins' lib.php files (including the one with the autoload require of repository_ocis.
* php public/admin/tool/phpunit/init.php
* Verify that phpunit.xml has NOT been created in content root, instead it has been built in public/repository/ocis
* When now running phpunit the phpunit.xml is not being found and an error occurs.

Similar issues will properly occur, if some autoloading is being done inside some autoloaded classes.

This also probably only happens, because repository_ocis registers itself with `$loader->register(true);` (repository/ocis/vendor/composer/autoload_real.php#34) which registers itself before the moodle root loader.
In {{InstalledVersions::getInstalled()::getRootPackage()}} the value {{$installed[0]}} then is not the moodle core loader but the repository_ocis one and phpunit.xml ends up being written to the wrong path.

So summing it up:

* Mainly, repository_ocis is doing a lot of bad things that lead to this issue. One could argue that this has to be fixed in the plugin.
* However, on the other hand, with the introduction of composer more and more plugins will continue to introduce composer and it’s maybe just a matter of time until there will be more plugins causing trouble.
* So I suggest to harden the core code to deal with such kind of things.



There is the same bug with behat:

{noformat}root@93d8f12357fa:/var/www/main# php public/admin/tool/behat/cli/init.php
You are already using the latest available Composer version 2.10.2 (stable channel).
Installing dependencies from lock file (including require-dev)
Verifying lock file contents can be installed on current platform.
Nothing to install, update or remove
Generating autoload files
70 packages you are using are looking for funding.
Use the `composer fund` command to find out more!
sh: 1: vendor/bin/behat: not found
Error: Error running behat CLI command. Try running "vendor/bin/behat --help" manually from CLI to find out more about the problem.
{noformat}

The shell exec command is using a path inside a plugin.

fields.description:
Some ESM bundles we want to load include the {{.js}} extension, for example Bootstrap’s {{bootstrap.js}} index looks like:


{code:javascript}export { default as Alert } from './src/alert.js'
export { default as Button } from './src/button.js'
export { default as Carousel } from './src/carousel.js'
export { default as Collapse } from './src/collapse.js'
export { default as Dropdown } from './src/dropdown.js'
export { default as Modal } from './src/modal.js'
export { default as Offcanvas } from './src/offcanvas.js'
export { default as Popover } from './src/popover.js'
export { default as ScrollSpy } from './src/scrollspy.js'
export { default as Tab } from './src/tab.js'
export { default as Toast } from './src/toast.js'
export { default as Tooltip } from './src/tooltip.js'{code}

Our current loader would require us to modify each of these includes to remove the {{.js}} in each of the export from statements.

So instead of automatically loading the {{.js}} file by automatically adding the suffix, the idea here is to allow the URL to include _certain_ suffixes, notably:

* {{.js}}

At the same time, by allowing {{.js.map}} we can also support source maps.

However, if it is included with other search/filtering-related controls, such as in the “Course overview” block, which also defines a search landmark for the container that contains the filtering and search controls. * 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (Level A): Landmark navigation becomes less effective when landmarks are nested or redundant

We should update the template so that the search landmark role can be removed/overridden when necessary.

fields.description:
Initially we went with a single build for the ESM outputs. In [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88786|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88786|smart-link] we simplified this build because it was generating different output depending on whether the build was run in watch mode or not - the watch would generate a ‘dev' build with some different options for minify, sourcemapping, etc.

Now we know we do not want a different built depending on how the code is built, but this did later raise the question of whether we wanted a dev build at all.

In our YUI days we generated three outputs:

* min.js - a minified version for production
* .js - a non-minified version for …????
* -debug.js - a non-minified version with debugging

We did away with this with AMD.

And now I feel like we should come back to it with our new React overlord as it has a number of benefits when it comes to React client-side tooling and management.

The advantages as I see it:

* React profiler can be enabled/disabled based on the version used
* Source maps can be provided to clients for Development only
* Various other development features can be enabled for development, including:
** jsxDev
** keepNames
** minify



Whilst an improvement we shoudl still backport this change, which is in keeping with the policy we have for AMD changes. I don’t anticipate many people using ESM in 5.2, but it is still supported.

I would also suggest that we rename the task from {{grunt react}} to {{grunt esm}} given this is not a react-specific task.

fields.summary: Backup file_logger should store relative paths

issuetype.description: An enhancement to an existing Moodle feature. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)
issuetype.name: Improvement

fields.description:
h2. Summary

Backup {{file_logger}} should serialize a relative path (just the filename) rather than the absolute {{$CFG->backuptempdir/$backupid.log}}. 

The absolute path is host specific and ends up baked into the backup controller record and into the {{.mbz}} artefact, which makes backups non portable and causes restore code to blindly open whatever path was deserialized. Storing a relative path and rebuilding the full path on the fly using the current {{$CFG->backuptempdir}} fixes both.

h2. Background

This came out of [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-76288|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-76288|smart-link], which fixed {{backup_cleanup_task}} crashing when {{$CFG->backuptempdir}} had changed since the controller was serialised. {{file_logger::__wakeup}} now needs to also handle relative paths, this ticket adds that read-side support alongside switching the writer to produce relative paths.

fields.description:
MDL-60912 (integrated in 5.0.7 / 5.1.4 / main) changed \core_completion\progress::get_course_progress_percentage() to call the new completion_info::get_user_activities_with_completion() instead of the lightweight get_activities().


For every course module with completion enabled, get_user_activities_with_completion() now constructs a \core_availability\info_module and calls filter_user_list(), which in turn calls capability_checker::get_users_by_capability('moodle/course:ignoreavailabilityrestrictions') on the module context.


This availability + capability resolution runs per module, per course, per request. On pages that summarise many courses via course_summary_exporter — Dashboard, Calendar block, Timeline block, Starred courses, My overview — the cost multiplies (courses × completion-enabled modules × capability resolution) and produces a noticeable performance regression compared with 5.0.6. The expensive work is also repeated because get_course_progress_percentage() is called multiple times per request for the same (course, user) pair (e.g. calendar/classes/external/event_exporter_base.php instantiates a new course_summary_exporter per event).


+*_This was anticipated during the MDL-60912 review (performance concern was raised in the comments) but no follow-up optimisation was integrated._*+



*Steps to reproduce*

# Site with completion tracking enabled.
# A user enrolled in many courses, each with several completion-tracked activities (with few or no availability/group restrictions — the common case).
# Load the Dashboard (or a page with the Calendar / Timeline / Starred courses blocks).
# Profile the request (e.g. $CFG->perfdebug = 15, or an APM/DB-query profiler).

Expected result
Course progress percentages are calculated with overhead comparable to 5.0.6; unrestricted activities do not incur per-module availability/capability resolution.


*Actual result*
Each completion-tracked module triggers an info_module + get_users_by_capability() resolution, repeated across courses and repeated per call within the same request, measurably increasing DB load and page render time.


*Affected code*

* completion/classes/progress.php — get_course_progress_percentage()
* lib/completionlib.php — get_user_activities_with_completion() (introduced by MDL-51447, used by MDL-60912)
* Callers via core_course\external\course_summary_exporter (Dashboard, block_calendar_*, block_timeline, block_starredcourses, block_myoverview, enrol/externallib.php, report builder completion formatter)



*Proposed solution*
Two complementary, behaviour-preserving optimisations (correctness of MDL-60912 fully retained):

# Fast path in get_user_activities_with_completion() — when a module has no availability rule (empty($cm->availability)), is not in separate-groups mode ($cm->groupmode !== SEPARATEGROUPS), and has no grouping restriction (empty($cm->groupingid)), the module is accessible to every enrolled user. Skip the info_module + capability_checker work and count it directly. This is mathematically equivalent to the existing slow path for unrestricted modules (the overwhelming majority). Modules that actually carry a restriction still take the full slow path, so hidden/unavailable/group-restricted activities continue to be excluded correctly.
# Per-request memoisation in get_course_progress_percentage() — cache the computed percentage per (course, user) in a MODE_REQUEST cache so repeated calls within one request (multiple exporters) reuse the result. Cheap pre-checks (is_enabled(), is_tracked_user()) stay outside the cache so capability/setting changes are always honoured. The cache key embeds $course->cacherev (so structural / visibility / availability / grouping changes invalidate it automatically), and the cache is purged in completion_info::internal_set_data() so completion-state changes within the same request are reflected.
No DB schema change, no version.php bump, no new cache definition, no new events/observers required.

Steps to reproduce

# Site with completion tracking enabled.
# A user enrolled in many courses, each with several completion-tracked activities (with few or no availability/group restrictions — the common case).
# Load the Dashboard (or a page with the Calendar / Timeline / Starred courses blocks).
# Profile the request (e.g. $CFG->perfdebug = 15, or an APM/DB-query profiler).



*At Moxis, we have already implemented a fix and it works. It keeps the fix from MDL-60912 but skips unnecessary steps and caches where relevant. I have added the patch for this issue as an attachment.*
